stories.title: Netanyahu scrambles for votes as Israelis turn out in record numbers
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, fighting for his political life, scrambled to bring out his base on Tuesday as Israelis voted in record numbers in the country’s first election since the Oct 7, 2023 attack.

With Israeli Arabs voters turning out in strong numbers, Netanyahu raised fears that leaders of the minority group were out to “steal the election” and reverse the hardline Jewish nationalist direction in which his government has taken the country.

The last opinion polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief.

stories.title: Govt raises threshold for currency transaction reports to Rs3m as anti-money laundering framework reviewed
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government has enhanced the currency transaction threshold by 50pc to Rs3 million for banks to trigger suspicious reports to the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU) of the State Bank of Pakistan under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA).

It serves as a strategic forum for strengthening Pakistan’s AML-CFT framework and ensuring timely coordination, inter-agency cooperation and consistent monitoring for effective implementation of the measures discussed.

The NEC also highlighted the importance of keeping Pakistan’s AML-CFT framework responsive to evolving financial risks and emerging technologies, while strengthening the analytical capabilities of relevant institutions.

stories.title: Govt to end slab system punishing power consumers crossing 200-unit threshold
summary: ISLAMABAD: Power Minister Awais Leghari told the Senate on Tuesday that the government has decided to scrap the electricity slab system that punishes consumers for crossing the 200-unit threshold even by one unit, and to provide targeted subsidy only to those deserving.
Under the current mechanism, consumers using up to 200 units per month fall under the “protected” category and avail a subsidy of around Rs13 per unit.

Speaking in the Upper House, Leghari said work was being expedited to abolish the system under which a consumer crossing 200 units has to pay a much higher cost per unit and remains ineligible for relief for the next six months.

stories.title: Justice Ayesha Malik challenges assumptions blaming women for 'inviting' rape
summary: The judge was addressing participants at the launch of a bench book on the adjudication of rape cases for judges of gender-based violence (GBV) courts in Islamabad.
The event was held in collaboration between the Ministry of Human Rights (MoHR), the Legal Aid Society (LAS) and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).

The bench book brings together applicable law and judicial guidance in 10 chapters following the sequence of a trial, and supports judges in assessing evidence that is placed before them, according to the rights ministry.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

stories.title: Brazil's Lula turns 81, vows to work '24 hours a day'
summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva turned 81 on Tuesday, promising to work “24 hours a day” following his historic re-election for a fourth term.
Lula won Sunday’s runoff against Flavio Bolsonaro with 51.8 per cent of the vote to the right-wing senator’s 48.2pc.
Following his shock first-round defeat to Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro, Lula’s campaign had a social media makeover.

stories.title: Joint JI-govt committee to mull ways to expand fuel relief scheme
summary: Rehman acknowledged that JI was aware of the fluctuations in international oil prices due to the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, but “we want relief to be provided to the people in this regard as well, and this levy should also be abolished alongside”.
Rehman on Monday warned that the party would march to Islamabad in mid-November if the premier did not abolish the petroleum levy.
On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

stories.title: In bid to boost exports, govt sets 120-day deadline for roadmap to expand shrimp farming
summary: ISLAMABAD: A sub-committee constituted by the prime minister has set a 120-day deadline to prepare a roadmap to expand shrimp farming, improve value addition and boost exports.
Maritime Affairs Minister Junaid Anwar Chaudhry on Tuesday chaired a meeting of the sub-committee on aquaculture and the shrimp value chain, according to a press release.
According to the statement, Chaudhry said the exercise would identify constraints and develop practical solutions to expand shrimp farming, strengthen value addition and increase exports.

stories.title: Karachi suspect accused of luring women for jobs, stealing their phones beaten with slippers during court appearance
summary: The suspect was arrested by the police on Monday for his alleged involvement in stealing the mobile phones of 59 women, who were brought to the farmhouse in October under the pretext of a job interview.
A day earlier, Malir Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Abdul Khaliq Pirzada told Dawn that the police had recovered 40 mobile phones from the suspect’s possession.
Pirzada said police had obtained clues suggesting that the remaining 19 mobile phones were in the possession of another absconding suspect.

stories.title: Rs930b Islamic funds curb debt
summary: The federal government has managed to execute an Islamic financing transaction of Rs930 billion to reduce the growing circular debt in the power sector.
At a public hearing held on Tuesday, the officials of Central Power Purchasing Agency-Guarantee (CPPA-G) made the revelation about the Shariah-compliant financing to curb the debt.

CPPA-G requested the power-sector regulator – the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) – to allow the company to file a Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) petition in the next financial year instead of requiring it to submit the application immediately.

stories.title: SMEs make up 99% of businesses, 78% of jobs
summary: Members of the SMEDA board had also been included in the committee, he said, to ensure institutional input and meaningful consultation in preparing the reform proposals.

The committee decided to examine international best practices and successful institutional models to develop a comprehensive and practical reorganisation plan tailored to Pakistan's economic and business environment.

Khan reaffirmed the government's commitment to transforming SMEDA into a more accessible, responsive and effective institution that could facilitate entrepreneurs, improve access to finance and promote business development across the country.

stories.title: 120 days given for shrimp roadmap
summary: The committee will prepare a comprehensive report based on verified data and stakeholder recommendations, establishing a baseline for the sector, identifying bottlenecks across the value chain and proposing measures to improve production, processing and export competitiveness.

Punjab Secretary for Aquaculture and Fisheries Rana Muhammad Saleem Afzal said the provincial government was working to expand shrimp farming, but establishing an effective value chain remained a major challenge, and efforts were under way to establish hatcheries.
Other participants presented proposals to improve shrimp processing, value addition and export competitiveness.

stories.title: Gold drops despite global gains on oil
summary: Gold prices in Pakistan declined on Tuesday, falling Rs1,300 per tola, despite a recovery in international markets, where bullion gained nearly 1% as softer oil prices eased inflation concerns ahead of the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy decision.

In the local market, gold prices settled at Rs422,136 per tola, while the price of 10-gram gold dropped Rs1,115 to Rs361,913, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association.
On Monday, gold prices had increased Rs1,400 per tola to Rs423,436.

stories.title: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after Oct 2025 truce
summary: Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October’s US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday.

Another report by the commission in September last year found that Israel had committed genocide ​in Gaza and that top Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, incited these acts — accusations that ⁠Israel called scandalous.

In its report to the UN General Assembly, the commission said the situation in the West Bank had also deteriorated sharply, with the number of Palestinians killed in airstrikes increasing from six between 2008 and Oct 6, 2023, to 254 between Oct 7, 2023 and Sept 30, 2026.

stories.title: Apple to replace iPhone Duo devices over reported screen problems
summary: Apple said it would replace iPhone Duo handsets affected by screen problems, just days after the highly anticipated foldable smartphone went on sale, the BBC reported on Tuesday.

Read: Apple's iPhone Duo faces early durability concerns as users report cracked screens Some owners also shared photos showing cracks along the screen’s central crease, while others reported hearing a crunching noise when opening the device.
Apple customers have reported cracks appearing on the screens of its new £2,000 foldable iPhone Duo, just weeks after the smartphone went on sale.

stories.title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic or existential' AI risks in IPO filing
summary: US artificial intelligence company Anthropic warned on Monday that its technology could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," citing concerns about increasingly autonomous AI systems that may act unpredictably or resist human oversight.

Read: AI models may soon self-replicate without access to data centres, Anthropic warns The company also warned that AI models, including its own, have demonstrated unexpected self-preserving behaviour, such as resisting attempts to shut them down.
The company said it and other researchers had raised concerns that advanced AI systems could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" if deployed without adequate safeguards.

stories.title: At least 1 killed, 7 injured as roof of under-construction building collapses in Multan
summary: LAHORE: At least one individual was killed, while seven others were injured on Tuesday when the roof of an under-construction building collapsed near Multan’s Northern Bypass, Rescue 1122 said.
In a statement, the rescue service said the roof of an under-construction plaza had collapsed near the National College of Business Administration and Economics on Northern Bypass.

Rescue officials launch a search and rescue operation after building collapse in Multan on October 27, 2026. — Photo via Rescue 1122 A rescue official confirmed to Dawn that eight labourers were present on the site when the incident occurred.

stories.title: New private equity policy framework on the horizon to bring over $10bn in investments
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government is set to roll out a new private equity policy framework covering enhanced risk portfolios, targeting $10 to $15 billion in tax-neutral investment from domestic and international players in the private equity market.
The meeting reviewed progress on regulatory and tax reforms, domestic capital mobilisation and the development of investment opportunities to support a robust private equity ecosystem in Pakistan.

Reviewing progress on regulatory reforms, the committee discussed measures concerning fund structures, transparency, investment arrangements and the participation of financial institutions in private equity funds.

stories.title: ATC reserves verdict in security breach case against Imaan, Hadi
summary: ISLAMABAD: The trial of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, in the security breach case concluded at Adiala Jail on Tuesday, with the anti-terrorism court (ATC) reserving its verdict.
A day prior, the couple approached the Supreme Court to challenge the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) Oct 19 order refusing to stay the trial in the case.
The couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the high court Bar Association president.

stories.title: SBP secure slim lead against MIT Solutions
summary: Batting first Markhor IT Solutions were bowled out for112 in 29.5 overs, with pacer Siraj Uddin and Shahid Aziz sharing the damage with the ball.
Siraj finished with 6-39 in nine overs, while Shahid claimed 4-39 in 7.5 overs to dismantle Markhor batting line-up.
Aitizaz Habib Khan top-scored for Markhor with 29 off 30 balls, smashing three fours and a six.

stories.title: Army destroys Afghan border check posts after 5 of a family injured, one killed in Angoor Adda: official
summary: The Pakistan Army on Tuesday night destroyed Afghan Taliban check posts after they targeted civilian areas in South Waziristan's Angoor Adda along the border, injuring five members of a family and killing one member.

In a post on X, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Information Adviser Samar Haroon Bilour, citing security sources, stated that "in the Angoor Adda area of South Waziristan, the Afghan Taliban regime, showing stubbornness, targeted the civilian population".
In a post on X, the South Waziristan deputy commissioner stated that the Afghan Taliban had engaged in "unprovoked" firing on civilian houses, further adding that many "shops were damaged".

stories.title: Bilawal calls for 'full stop' on conversations about new provinces
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Tuesday called for a “full stop” to conversations regarding the creation of new provinces.
However, since Naqvi’s remarks, various political parties have also spoken in favour of it and called for the creation of more provinces or administrative units for better governance.
The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) — an ally of the PML-N-led ruling coalition — has been demanding that Karachi be designated a province separate from Sindh.

stories.title: Two charged with security offences over plot at UK airbase used by US
summary: UK anti-terrorism police said on Tuesday that two men have been charged with national security offences after an incident last month at a British airbase used by the United States, linking the scare to Iran.
This is the first time that anyone has been charged over the incident at RAF Fairford, after police arrested seven suspects in the days afterwards, before releasing them on bail.
Suspects charged A week ago police said they had re-arrested two of the suspects, one of whom has now been charged.

stories.title: Pakistan’s child protection system failing to address online sexual abuse: HRCP
summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) warned on Tuesday that online sexual abuse of children remained a serious child protection concern, with underreporting, weak institutional coordination and inadequate safeguards preventing many cases from coming to light.
In its report on online child sexual abuse, the commission said the issue must be treated not merely as a cybercrime challenge but as a violation of children’s fundamental rights, dignity and safety.

According to a report launched by the National Commission on the Rights of the Child in collaboration with UNICEF Pakistan in September, around 1.5 million internet-using Pakistani children aged 12 to 17 were subjected to sexual exploitation and abuse online in a single year.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs3.19, increases diesel by Rs2.25 for Oct 28
summary: The federal government on Tuesday decreased the price of petrol by Rs3.19 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.25 per litre for October 28.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.54 and Rs2.16 per litre, respectively, for October 27.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral image of Saudi defence minister kissing Iranian president's hand is AI-generated
summary: On Oct 26, a Houthi supporter, based on their past posts, shared an image on X allegedly showing Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman kissing the hand of the Iranian president.

A keyword search was conducted to determine whether any credible Saudi, Iranian, or international media outlets had published the image or reported on an incident in which the Saudi defence minister allegedly kissed the Iranian president’s hand, but yielded no reports.
Therefore, the claim that a viral image shows the Saudi defence minister kissing the hand of the Iranian president is false.

stories.title: Madushanka’s five-for powers Sri Lanka into tri-series final after Pakistan drubbing
summary: Sri Lanka stormed into the final of the One-day International tri-series after overwhelming Pakistan by eight wickets, chasing a modest target of 111 in just 18.1 overs at the Gaddafi Stadium on Tuesday.

Left-arm pacer Dilshan Madushanka delivered a career-best five for 34 to dismantle Pakistan for 110 in 25.3 overs before Kamindu Mendis struck an unbeaten 62 to guide Sri Lanka to 114-2, sealing victory with 31.5 overs to spare.
The Pakistan captain’s brief counterattack included two sixes, but he was caught by Wellalage as Madushanka completed his five-wicket haul.

stories.title: Lahore ATC denies police further remand of PTI's Hammad Azhar, sends him on judicial remand
summary: LAHORE: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday rejected a police request for further physical remand of PTI leader Hammad Azhar in the Jinnah House attack case and sent him to jail on judicial remand.
The investigating officer sought further physical remand of the former finance minister, stating that the police wanted to conduct a polygraph test, also known as a lie detector test.

After hearing arguments from the prosecution and the defence over the proposed polygraph test, Judge Akram dismissed the police request for further physical remand and sent Azhar to jail under judicial custody.

stories.title: Prince of Kalat, three guards kidnapped in Balochistan
summary: Prince Muhammad Khan Ahmedzai, son of Khan of Kalat Mir Suleman Dawood Jan Ahmedzai, was reportedly abducted along with his three guards by unidentified suspects while travelling between Soorab and Kalat in Balochistan, sources said on Tuesday.
The incident reportedly took place last night when Prince Ahmedzai was travelling from Khuzdar to Kalat.

Read: Princely Liaisons: The Khan family controls politics in Kalat Following the incident, police, security agencies and other law enforcement authorities have launched efforts to trace the abducted men and secure their safe recovery.

stories.title: Naqvi hints at Imran's transfer to Islamabad’s new Model Jail
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi hinted on Tuesday that incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan could be shifted to a new jail in Islamabad.
He said he had inspected the jail's kitchen and hospital during the visit, adding that prisoners currently held in Islamabad would be shifted to the new facility after inauguration by the premier.
Once completed, it will become the first purpose-built prison for the federal capital, replacing the existing arrangement under which Islamabad's prisoners are housed at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail.

stories.title: At UNGA debate, Pakistan warns against adding more permanent members to Security Council, extending veto privileges
summary: Pakistan has warned that adding more permanent members to the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and extending veto privileges would “deepen existing inequalities, perpetuate historical advantages and increase the risk of Council paralysis”.

He called for a balanced approach combining restrictions on veto use with enhanced representation and a stronger role for elected members of the UNSC, making its decision-making “more democratic and providing an effective check on the exercise of veto power”.

A recent UN report has also warned that the veto power of the five permanent members of the Security Council is one of the reasons multilateral mechanisms have been unable to prevent or stop the growing number of state-based conflicts.

stories.title: Pakistan, China launch information corridor 'CPIC' to counter misleading narratives, promote cultural exchange
summary: Pakistan and China have launched the China-Pakistan Information Corridor (CPIC), with Information Minister Ataullah Tarar saying that the initiative will focus on countering misleading narratives, cultural exchanges and cooperation between think tanks.
And here too, Pakistan walks with China,” Tarar said.
The information minister, in his address, also invited Chinese media houses, think tanks, universities, enterprises, and youth ambassadors to join each pillar of CPIC.

stories.title: Indian court orders takedown of documentary on billionaire Gautam Adani, PM Modi
summary: An Indian court has ordered the takedown of an online documentary posted by Hotmail co-founder Sabeer Bhatia accusing Prime ​Minister Narendra Modi and billionaire Gautam Adani of cronyism, after Adani Enterprises sued, calling it defamatory.

In its challenge, Adani Enterprises told the court ​that it does not seek to restrain constructive criticism of government policy or of business concentration, but Bhatia had suppressed material facts, according to the court order.

Ahead of the court challenge, police in the state of Maharashtra, which is led by Modi’s ruling alliance, sent a takedown notice to Bhatia on October 19, saying the content “made serious unsubstantiated allegations”.

stories.title: No pressure from US to cut Russian oil imports, says Indian oil minister
summary: India has faced no pressure from ​the US to reduce its Russian crude ‌imports, oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Tuesday at an industry event. “I never felt anything,” Puri said when ​asked if there has been pressure to ​cut Russian oil imports.
He said India ​was getting 0.2 per cent of its oil imports from Russia before the Ukraine war, while imports have surged since the war ​started due to discounts on Russian oil.

India’s imports ​of Middle Eastern crude oil surged in September, returning to pre-war ‌levels, ⁠while its refiners cut back purchases of Russian oil amid stiff competition from China, ship-tracking data showed.

stories.title: Turkish parliament committee approves Makkah Agreement on joint defence with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
summary: The Turkish parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee on Tuesday approved a bill to ratify the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.
The bill was approved following deliberations during which Deputy Foreign Minister Levent Gumrukcu answered lawmakers' questions about the agreement.
Deal ‘envisions integration rather than bloc-building in region’ Gumrukcu stressed that the agreement was entirely defensive in nature and did not target any country.

stories.title: Pakistan reaffirms solidarity with Kashmiris on Black Day, calls for end to rights violations
summary: He called on the international community to fulfil its responsibilities towards the Kashmiri people, take sustained notice of the human rights situation in IIOJK and urge India to end rights violations and allow them to exercise their right to self-determination.

Dar said a just, peaceful and lasting resolution of the dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people was essential for peace and stability in South Asia.

NA resolution urges sustained diplomatic efforts The National Assembly also unanimously passed a resolution, reaffirming Pakistan’s “unwavering moral, political and diplomatic support” for the people of Jammu and Kashmir and their inalienable right to self-determination.

stories.title: Australia fight back in decisive Test
summary: Opener Marques Ackerman struck a career-best 95 and Aiden Markram made 78 as South Africa reached 221-4 at tea on the opening day of the third Test against Australia at Newlands on Tuesday.
Earlier, Australia made four changes after their innings and 31-run defeat in the second Test at Gqeberha, bringing in Cameron Green, wicket-keeper Josh Inglis, Connolly and Lyon.
The three-match Test series is level at 1-1 after Australia won the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs before South Africa responded emphatically in Gqeberha.

stories.title: Bilawal floats end to further debate on administrative units in Sindh
summary: Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Tuesday said the Sindh Assembly had already made its decision on the issue of further administrative units in the province and the debate should now be put to rest.

Debate over new administrative units in Sindh The debate over new administrative units in Sindh centres on whether creating smaller, empowered units would improve governance or threaten the province’s territorial integrity.
The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) strongly opposes any move to divide Sindh or alter its territorial boundaries.

stories.title: Bombay High Court pauses actor Imran Khan's exit notice until November 2
summary: An Indian court allowed Bollywood actor Imran Khan ‌to remain in the country until at least November 2, local media said on Tuesday, pausing a government order that asked him to leave for breaching immigration laws by allegedly participating in a protest.
Khan, 43, is a US ​citizen and was asked to leave the country by October 28 after he was accused of ​joining protests in Mumbai against the country's election chief this month.
Khan appealed against the order in the Bombay High Court, saying it was unconstitutional and arbitrary, ​local media reported.

stories.title: Humayun Saeed calls for Pakistan's own OTT platform to take dramas global
summary: Humayun Saeed believes Pakistani dramas deserve greater international visibility, including on streaming platforms such as Netflix, but says the country needs to develop its own over-the-top (OTT) platform to help local productions reach wider audiences.

Speaking about the possibility of Pakistani dramas reaching Netflix, Saeed said local productions had a distinct identity, particularly in their writing, dialogue delivery and use of Urdu. “Our dramas have a specific style.

Acknowledging that OTT productions often adopt a different, edgier approach, Saeed maintained that existing Pakistani dramas could still find an audience on international streaming platforms. “If you are saying the dramas we have already made should go on Netflix, then yes.
